settings.question: What's the difference between Open Sole and Closed Sole?
settings.answer:
Open Sole: Heel exposed, mid-foot breathing hole. More grounded, barefoot feel. Natural toe splay.

Closed Sole: Heel and foot fully covered.

Both perform identically — same grip, same stability, same studio uses. Choice is preference and feel only. Both deliver the same patented 360° grip, natural toe splay, and cost $74.

settings.question: Which style is better for reformer?
settings.answer: Either. Both soles perform identically across barre, reformer Pilates, Lagree, and Megaformer — same grip, same stability, same studio uses. Choice is preference and feel only.

settings.question: Which disciplines work with Performance Skins?
settings.answer: Barre, Reformer Pilates, Lagree, Megaformer, Cadillac, Mat Pilates, and Yoga. The 360° grip holds on all standard studio surfaces including reformer carriages, Megaformer platforms, and wood/rubber floors.

settings.question: Do they work for hot yoga?
settings.answer: Yes, with a thin sock recommended for sweat absorption in heated environments. The grip performs well on yoga surfaces in both regular and heated settings.

settings.question: What surfaces do Performance Skins work on?
settings.answer: Exceptional on all studio surfaces: reformer carriages, Megaformer platforms, wood floors, rubber mats, and yoga mats. Also works on beach, paddleboard, and boat surfaces. Certain wet tile and stone areas are inherently slippery for any footwear.

settings.question: Are Performance Skins designed to be worn barefoot?
settings.answer: Yes. They're built for direct skin contact — the material is skin-safe and non-toxic, with no latex and no silicone. Because it's non-porous, it stays clean without a sock barrier.

settings.question: Can I wear socks underneath?
settings.answer: A thin sock works well for: perspiration management, personal hygiene preference, or narrow feet that need a snugger fit. Skip thick socks — they reduce the grip connection and alter the fit.

settings.question: What are Performance Skins made of?
settings.answer:
A proprietary grip material — skin-safe and non-toxic, with no latex and no silicone. Made in the USA.

The surface is non-porous, so it doesn't soak up sweat the way fabric does. Rinse clean after every use.

settings.question: How should my Performance Skins fit?
settings.answer:
Feet are different, so this varies. Generally they should feel secure — not pinching, and not sliding around on your foot.

The material stretches and conforms to your foot, so depending on your foot shape and width that can feel close and snug or more relaxed. Both are fine. There's no break-in period — how they feel on day one is how they feel.

To place them: the ball of your foot sits where your foot meets your toes. Gently adjust the top edge at the ankle.

settings.question: Do certain colors fit differently?
settings.answer:
Slightly. Black and Light Grey are the most forgiving, especially for wider feet. Hot Coral, Dark Shadow, Dark Grey, and Blue fit snugger.

If you're right between sizes in one of the snugger colors, take the Large.

settings.question: What if I'm between sizes?
settings.answer:
Go by width. Right at the overlap between Medium and Large: wider foot → Large, narrower foot → Medium.

Color matters too. Black and Light Grey are the most forgiving for wider feet. Hot Coral, Dark Shadow, Dark Grey, and Blue fit snugger.

Still unsure? Contact us with your usual shoe size and we'll tell you which one to take.

settings.question: I have narrow feet — any tips?
settings.answer:
Take the Medium if you're between sizes, and consider one of the snugger colors — Hot Coral, Dark Shadow, Dark Grey, or Blue.

A thin sock underneath also works well for a more secure fit, and for anyone who prefers a barrier between skin and material.

settings.question: How do I clean my Performance Skins?
settings.answer:
Warm soapy water, rinse, air dry. That's it — no machine washing needed.

Because the surface is non-porous, sweat sits on it rather than soaking in the way it does with fabric. A quick rinse after class is usually all it takes to keep them fresh. When you wipe down your equipment, a pass with the same cloth works too.

settings.question: Can I machine wash them?
settings.answer: Hand wash with warm soapy water — it's better for longevity. The non-porous surface doesn't hold sweat the way fabric does, so a quick rinse after class is usually all you need.

settings.question: How should I put them on and take them off?
settings.answer: Pull from the top opening, not the straps. When removing, peel from the heel area. This preserves the strap attachment points and extends the life of your pair.

settings.question: How long do Performance Skins last?
settings.answer: Longevity varies by use frequency and intensity. Many customers report 3-4 years of use at 6 days per week. The injection-molded grip never peels or flakes — it's part of the sole itself.

settings.question: Will the grip wear off over time?
settings.answer: No. Unlike silicone dots on grip socks, our grip is injection-molded directly into the sole. It cannot peel, flake, or separate. The material maintains its shape and grip pattern throughout its lifespan.

settings.question: Do they lose shape after many uses?
settings.answer: No. The structured, injection-molded sole holds its shape — it doesn't stretch out the way fabric grip socks do after a few dozen washes.
